review_notes: I read the whole file and compared the repeated-looking blocks: the symmetric hux/hxv, hlu/hvs and hvq/hqu pieces in exists_orderedBox_subset_open; the `Set.mem_iUnion` destructuring in hinter, hKt, htU and htS; and the ext1/grw/by_cases pattern in the two indicatorConstLp lemmas. All of these are short or routine unfolding, so I did not report them. The one real duplication is the sup'/inf' bound argument in exists_orderedBox_biInter. A grep of the Malliavin directory shows this argument appears only in this file, and only in that one proof. So the repeat is two blocks in a single proof, not two separate declarations. The rewrite below is a sketch I have not compiled. It is the only finding I am confident in.

findings.problem: The argument that a point of the intersection satisfies sup' u < y i ≤ inf' v is written out twice, once for the witness z (huz/hzv, lines 149-157) and once for the arbitrary y in the first inclusion (hui/hvi, lines 171-181). Each copy does the same `Finset.sup'_lt_iff` and `Finset.le_inf'` reasoning. They differ only in how membership in each box is extracted: `hzb` for z, and a nested `Set.mem_iInter.mp` for y. The `hzb` helper exists only for the first copy.
findings.proposed_change:
Prove the bound once for every point of the intersection, before `hvalid`, and use it for both z and y. Sketch (uncompiled):

have hbound : ∀ y ∈ (⋂ b ∈ s, orderedBox b.u b.v), ∀ i, u i < y i ∧ y i ≤ v i := by
  intro y hy i
  have hyb : ∀ b ∈ s, y ∈ orderedBox b.u b.v := fun b hb => Set.mem_iInter₂.mp hy b hb
  refine ⟨?_, Finset.le_inf' hs _ fun b hb => (hyb b hb i (Set.mem_univ i)).2⟩
  simp only [u]
  rw [Finset.sup'_lt_iff]
  exact fun b hb => (hyb b hb i (Set.mem_univ i)).1

Then `hvalid := fun i => ((hbound z hz i).1.le).trans (hbound z hz i).2`. The first inclusion becomes `fun y hy i _ => hbound y hy i`. This removes `hzb`, `huz`, `hzv`, `hui` and `hvi`.
findings.benefit: The sup'/inf' bound is stated and proved once, so a reader checks one lemma instead of two near-identical blocks. Any change, such as a different box convention (Ioc to Ico), is made in one place. About 20 lines shrink to about 8.
